newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan airline orders two Boeing 737-800s.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan airline orders two Boeing 737-800s.

text.p: Morocco's state airline Royal Air Maroc has ordered two new generation Boeing 737-800s for delivery in April 1998, an airline spokesman said on Monday.
The planes will be used on medium haul routes, mainly Europe, Africa and Middle East destinations like Egypt, the company said.
"This decision is part of the development strategy for the medium haul market, notably European, of Royal Air Maroc...," it added.
"Royal Air Maroc will be one of the first companies to exploit this new aircraft which will be equipped with two CFM 56-FB engines."
The aircraft will be configured to have 24 luxury class seats and 129 economy class.
The company did not disclose the price of the two planes.
Royal Air Maroc at present operates 27 aircraft, mainly Boeings, and made a net profit of 74 million dirhams ($8.5 million) in the first eight months of 1996, carrying 1.8 million passengers.
